newsitem.title: INDIA: Peregrine's Purker's reaction to Indian flux.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine's Purker's reaction to Indian flux.

text.p: Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Capital India Pvt Ltd, on Saturday gave Reuters the following view on Indian markets after the United Front alliance was defeated in a confidence motion and a search for a new coalition got underway.
"The numbers don't appear to add up very easily."
"The BJP won't get support and neither will Congress."
"Mid-term elections look to have an equal or more probable chance (than a new coalition being formed)."
He also said any new coalition was unlikely to last long, unlikely to take tough decisions, and could pander to populism.
"Expenditure controls are likely to go on the backburner."
"One good thing is that the budget seems to be accepted."
He said if the budget is passed investment houses could leave intact their earnings estimates for companies based on new fiscal policies."
"It is a little premature to predict ranges. But in the short-term, one or two months, there is not too much upside."
He said at current levels the market was discounting the optimistic scenario, of a passed budget and new coalition, more than the pessimistic scenario, of a plunge into mid-term elections."
